Recently the beacon flickered green for a heartbeat. Green is not a signal anyone knows. Aldous denies it happened, but half the harbor saw it.

75.comment: The Temple of Valkur — Windcaller's Pier
75.content:
At the Temple of Valkur, Windcaller's Pier, sailors pray for safe passage through the Narrow Pass. The temple is built at the end of the longest pier, a weathered round building of grey stone and driftwood topped by a tall mast flying blue pennants. Its open sides let the sea wind through, and its floor is a great compass rose of colored tiles. The walls are covered with offerings: carved model ships, knotted ropes, coins nailed to the timbers, and the names of the drowned.
Sailors pray here before every voyage and leave a coin "for the Captain" on return. Priests of Valkur bless ships, read the weather, and sometimes sail with crews through dangerous waters. On the Day of Drowned Lanterns, the whole city gathers along the pier. The temple is led by Windcaller Morwen Salt.

76.content:
Harbormaster Rowan Greaves (human, 50) runs Breakwater Docks and the Pass toll office. He is stocky and weather-beaten, with a red face, a bristling ginger-grey beard, a gold hoop in one ear, and a loud voice that carries over the gulls. He wears a blue harbor coat with brass buttons, often undone, and carries a brass spyglass on a cord.
Personality: harried, gruff, honest, and overworked. He takes pride in running a clean harbor in a dirty trade and is frustrated by underpaid inspectors, crooked nobles, and endless Valerian complaints. He likes plain dealers and pays decently for help.
Speech: loud, harried, salty. "Toll's posted, Captain. Pay it, argue it, or sail into the Shoals for all I care. Next!"
Current concern: toll revenue is down, smuggled goods are everywhere, and wreck-lights have been seen on the Broken Shoals. He suspects a hidden channel through the Shoals and someone powerful protecting it. He is hiring discreet investigators.
Secret: his younger brother is a Sewer Rat smuggler. Rowan has covered for him twice and dreads the day he will have to choose.

77.content:
Captain Saoirse Deane (half-elf, 44) is guildmaster of the Mariner's Guild and captain of the merchant ship Gale's Daughter. She is tall and rangy, with sun-darkened skin, freckles, wind-tangled black hair streaked with grey, and a long sea coat. She wears a cutlass she has used more than once and has a laugh that fills a room.
Personality: bold, generous, and fiercely protective of sailors. She has sailed every route from the North Sea to the far south and around the Broken Shoals more times than she can count. She has no patience for nobles or toll clerks, and enormous patience for green deckhands.
Speech: hearty, colorful, full of sea-talk. "The sea takes the careless, love, and the clever, and the unlucky, so we keep our wits sharp and our luck sharper."
Role: hires crews, settles disputes between sailors, knows every ship and captain in port, and can arrange passage anywhere.
Secret: she is a former privateer who raided Valerian shipping during the Pass War under a royal letter of marque. Valerius still has a price on her head under another name, and Envoy Dravon has just learned who she is.

78.content:
Aldous Merrow (human, 69) is the Beacon-Keeper of the Narrow Pass Watchtower. He has tended the blue flame for forty years. He is thin and stooped, with wispy white hair, a long nose, watery blue eyes, and thick spectacles. He wears a faded army coat over a woolen robe and is never without a battered ledger in which he records every ship, storm, and change in the flame.
Personality: gentle, fussy, lonely, and devoted to his duty. He talks to the flame as if it were a friend and to visitors as if they were the flame. He loves tea, gulls, and long stories about the beacon's history, and he is rarely believed.
Speech: quavering, rambling, precise about details. "Forty years, and not one wrong color. Not one. Blue for peace, red for war, white for wreck. There's no green, you see. There isn't a green."
Current situation: he swears the beacon never flickered green. In truth he saw it and is terrified. When it happened, he felt a cold presence in the tower and heard stone grinding beneath the floor.
Secret: his ledger has recorded three more green flickers that no one else saw, each on a night when the First Flame in the Temple of Helm also guttered.

79.content:
Windcaller Morwen Salt (human, 40) leads the Temple of Valkur at Windcaller's Pier. She is tall and strong, with deeply tanned skin, wild sea-grey hair full of beads and shells, and pale eyes that seem always to look at the horizon. Her arms are covered in tattoos of waves and ships, and she wears a sealskin cloak and a whistle carved from whalebone.
Personality: wild, intense, and joyful. She is a sailor first and a priestess second, and she prefers the deck of a ship to the temple. She can read the weather like a book and calls the wind with her whistle. She speaks with the dead at sea and is unafraid of anything except ships that sail without a blessing.
Speech: rhythmic, poetic, full of sea lore. "The sea doesn't care if you're good, sailor, only if you're ready. Give the Captain his coin and keep your knife sharp."
Role: blesses ships, sails with crews through dangerous waters, and keeps the names of the drowned.
Secret: she has been hearing the drowned of the Broken Shoals singing, calling her name. She believes something has woken beneath the reefs, and that the moving lanterns there are not carried by the living.

80.content:
The Undercity ("Secrets, shadows, and illegal markets") is the hidden layer beneath Skyreach: drains, cisterns, old foundations, forgotten cellars, abandoned servants' passages, and natural caves in the granite spur. Some tunnels are six centuries old; others are older than the city itself. Officially it is a sewer system maintained by the Wardens of each district. In practice it belongs to the Sewer Rats.
It is dark, damp, and echoing. Air smells of wet stone, rot, lamp oil, and the sea. Dangers include flooding at high tide, collapses, giant rats, the occasional otyugh, Sentinel raids, and the Rats themselves. Entrances are hidden in cellars across the Winding Ways, in warehouse floors at the harbor, inside the hollow pillar of the Coilstone Steps, and (rumor says) beneath the Noble Quarter. Main places include the Ratway, the Underflow Market, and the Gutter Throne. Rumors also speak of deeper places: sealed stone doors carved with eyes, which even the Rats will not open.

81.content:
The Ratway is a network of tunnels lit by dim lanterns that connect the different areas of the city. It is mostly patrolled by the Sewer Rats, the thieves' guild. Its main passages follow the great drains beneath the Winding Ways and the Harbor District, with walkways along filthy channels, ladders up into cellars, and rope bridges over flooded shafts. Lanterns hang at junctions, shuttered or lit to signal safety or danger. Chalk rat-tails mark the way: curled for safe, straight for danger, crossed for Sentinels.
Anyone may use the Ratway, but outsiders pay a toll (usually a silver eye) to Rat sentries or are guided, robbed, or lost. The Rats run smuggled goods through it from the harbor to the Underflow Market, and they move people as well: fugitives, spies, and anyone else who needs to cross the city unseen. Unmapped side passages lead into older, stranger tunnels, and Rats who explore too deep sometimes don't come back.

82.content:
Black-market goods, stolen items, and illegal magic are moved through makeshift markets set up in the underground tunnels of the Ratway. The Underflow Market moves every few nights between the large chambers of the Ratway (an old cistern, a collapsed cellar, a drained reservoir), and finding it requires a Rat guide, a password, or a chalk-sign trail. Stalls are crates and blankets lit by candles; buyers wear hoods or masks; and the only law is the Rats' law.
Goods for sale include stolen jewelry, smuggled wine and spices, untaxed Skyreach steel (lately including Iron Works pieces), poisons, forged Writs of Passage and silver eyes, Valerian contraband, salvage from wrecks on the Broken Shoals, curse-scrolls, and forbidden tomes. Prices are high and haggling is expected. Fighting is forbidden and punished by the Rats, but pickpocketing is a sport. Mister Penny, the Rats' fence, presides.

83.content:
The Gutter Throne occupies a half-flooded cistern where old drainage channels converge beneath the city. Crude walkways lead to a raised stone platform assembled from broken masonry, stolen furnishings, and rusted ironwork, the seat from which the Sewer Rats settle disputes and divide their profits. Every approach is watched, every whisper carries across the water, and visitors are never allowed to forget that the gang knows more routes out of the chamber than they do.
The throne itself is a huge carved chair stolen from a noble house generations ago, its arms reinforced with iron and its back decorated with rat skulls and stolen crowns. Lanterns hang from chains above the water, and the floor of the cistern is lost in darkness; traitors are given "a swim" here. Old Tallow, the aging leader of the Rats, holds court here every night, with his lieutenants Vex and Mister Penny on either side and Kael Broker lounging nearby, usually with news no one else has heard yet. Petitioners must bring a gift.

84.content:
Old Tallow (human, 71) is the boss of the Sewer Rats and sits the Gutter Throne. He is a vast, pale, flabby man with tiny bright eyes sunk in a doughy face, a few strands of white hair, and fingers covered in stolen rings. He wears a filthy velvet robe over layers of furs and is surrounded at all times by candles, which he makes himself from tallow (hence the name). He can no longer walk far, and he coughs blood into silk handkerchiefs.
Personality: genial, avuncular, sentimental, and utterly ruthless. He has ruled the Rats for thirty years, kept worse gangs out of Skyreach, and fed half the Winding Ways in hard winters. He speaks fondly of "my children" and drowns traitors without raising his voice. He knows he is dying.
Speech: wheezing, warm, and menacing. "Come closer, sweetling. Old Tallow doesn't bite. He has people for that."
Current concern: who will succeed him? He doesn't trust Vex, and he doesn't have time to find anyone else.
Secret: he has been selling information to the Keeper of Whispers for twenty years in exchange for the Sentinels' tolerance. If the Rats learned of it, they would give him a swim.

85.content:
Vex (tiefling, 31) is Old Tallow's chief lieutenant and the most feared Sewer Rat in Skyreach. She is lithe and sharp-featured, with dusky violet skin, swept-back horns capped in silver, long black hair, and golden eyes. She dresses in fitted black leather and a hooded cloak, with half a dozen knives hidden on her. Her tail is never still.
Personality: cold, clever, ambitious, and charismatic. She grew up on the streets of the Winding Ways, despised as a tiefling, and clawed her way up through the Rats. She wants more than the Gutter Throne; she wants the Rats to be a power in Skyreach that nobles must bow to. She is ruthless, but she keeps her word.
Speech: low, amused, dangerous. "Everyone in this city owes someone, darling. I just make sure they owe me."
Activities: she runs the Coliseum betting and the smuggling route through the Broken Shoals. She holds Lord Damon Vantor's debts and Kestrel Dane's.
Secret: Vex is ready to take the Gutter Throne the moment Old Tallow dies, or sooner. She is quietly in contact with Twinharbor's Underwave Syndicates, which have offered to back her in exchange for a cut of the Pass smuggling.

86.content:
Mister Penny (halfling, 60) is the Sewer Rats' fence and presides over the Underflow Market. He is small, tidy, and bald, with round spectacles, a neat grey mustache, and an immaculate (if outdated) brown suit. He carries a jeweler's loupe on a chain and a ledger in which he records every transaction in a private code.
Personality: polite, precise, fussy, and entirely amoral. He treats crime as a business and his customers as clients. He never haggles rudely, never threatens, and never forgets a debt. He has a weakness for fine pastries and rare books.
Speech: courteous, clerical, prim. "Twelve crowns, ten eyes. A fair price, given the provenance. I shall not ask about the blood on the clasp. Do mind it on the carpet."
Role: buys and sells stolen goods, appraises magic items, launders coin, and arranges forged documents.
Secret: Mister Penny's ledger is the most dangerous book in Skyreach. It records every noble, Sentinel, and merchant who has bought from or sold to the Rats, including the buyer who has been purchasing forged silver eyes in bulk (an Ashgrove servant). He is quietly undecided whether to back Vex or someone else when Tallow dies.

87.content:
Kael Broker (human, 28) is the Sewer Rats' dealmaker, the smooth face the guild shows to anyone above ground. Nobles, merchants, ship captains, and the occasional Sentinel who want something done quietly end up talking to Kael. He is handsome and lean, with dark hair swept back, a neatly trimmed beard, and clever hazel eyes that are always measuring. He wears fancy-looking leather armor: supple black-dyed leather tooled with silver filigree, a high collar, polished buckles, and a short cape. He looks more like a young lord's duelist than a thief. A slim rapier and at least two hidden knives complete the look.
Personality: slick, confident, charming, and always three steps ahead. He usually knows more than whoever he is talking to, and he enjoys letting them find that out slowly. He treats every conversation as a negotiation and every person as either an asset or a liability. He is rarely rude and never in a hurry. Underneath the polish is a Winding Ways kid who clawed his way out of the gutter and does not intend to go back.
Speech: smooth, amused, and knowing, often answering a question with a better one. "Relax. I'm not here to rob you. I'm here to tell you who already has, and what it'll cost to get it back."
Role: brokers the Rats' deals above ground, including protection contracts, smuggling arrangements, the Coliseum betting books, and favors for nobles. He arranged Lord Damon Vantor's toll-dodging route through the Broken Shoals, and he works the Gilded Gull and Sapphire Hall's servants' entrance as comfortably as the Gutter Throne. He has a network of street runners (dockhands, Coliseum vendors, and pages in noble houses) who feed him gossip.
Connections: Old Tallow treats him like a favored nephew; Vex considers him useful and dangerous; Mister Penny admires his manners; Jory Malloy is his friendly rival in the information trade. He used to run with Gorm Stoneheart and still calls him "big brother." He trusts no one, but he trusts Gorm least badly.
Secret: everyone assumes Kael will back Vex when Old Tallow dies. In truth he kept a signed copy of the Vantor smuggling agreement as insurance and has been quietly gathering leverage on half the guild. He intends to be the kingmaker of the succession, or to take the Gutter Throne himself if the price is right.

88.content:
The Deep Woods Gate district ("The forest watches") is the southern edge of Skyreach, where the city walls meet the forest road to Twinharbor. It is a small, rough district of stables, wagon yards, outfitters, cheap inns, and guide offices clustered around the massive Southern Gate. Beyond the walls, cleared ground runs about a bowshot before the Deep Woods rise like a dark wall.
Caravans assemble here for crossings, and the air smells of horses, pine, pitch, and woodsmoke. Everyone here keeps one eye on the tree line. Bells hang from every eave, and locals never whistle after dark (it is said the forest whistles back). Notable places include the Southern Gate Checkpoint, the Trailhouse, and the Shrine of Silvanus.

89.content:
The Southern Gate Checkpoint marks the last orderly ground before the road enters the Deep Woods. Guards inspect wagons beneath iron lanterns while licensed guides study weather, tracks, and the uneasy tree line beyond the walls. Travelers gather here to hire protection, register their routes, and hear the latest warnings; those returning from the forest are questioned just as carefully as those preparing to enter it.
The gate is a heavy double portcullis set in a fortified gatehouse, flanked by towers where archers watch the forest day and night. Every traveler entering the Woods must register their names, route, and expected return at the Guides' Registry. Returners are counted, questioned, and examined by a priest of Helm; it is whispered that sometimes more people come back than went in. The gate closes at sunset and opens at dawn without exception. The checkpoint is commanded by Gate Captain Ilse Torvald.

90.content:
The Trailhouse is a small outpost for guides and travelers. It is a sturdy log-and-stone lodge just inside the Southern Gate, with a sod roof, a ring of iron bells hung around the porch, and a great stone hearth that never goes cold. It serves as an inn, supply post, and gathering place for guides, rangers, hunters, and caravan guards.
Travelers can buy trail supplies (rope, lanterns, salt, iron nails, forest bells, rations), rent a bunk, and listen to the latest news from the Woods. A wall map of the forest road is covered with pins and notes in many hands. Returning guides leave warnings on it: "Path shifted at Hollow Oak," "Voices near the creek," "Don't answer." The Trailhouse is run by ranger Wren Ashby.

91.comment: The Shrine of Silvanus — Rootfather's Stone
91.content:
The Shrine of Silvanus, Rootfather's Stone, is a moss-covered altar where travelers leave offerings. It stands just outside the Southern Gate at the edge of the cleared ground, a huge boulder half-swallowed by the roots of an ancient oak. The stone is carved with faint spirals worn almost smooth, and offerings of bread, salt, coins, ribbons, and carved wooden animals are piled at its base. Travelers leave something here before entering the Woods "so the forest knows you asked."
The shrine predates the city. It is tended by a druid called Old Moss, who lives in a hut among the roots and rarely enters the city. Travelers who skip the offering are considered fools, and guides will not take them.

92.content:
Gate Captain Ilse Torvald (human, 42) commands the Southern Gate Checkpoint. She is solid and square-jawed, with cropped dark-blond hair, a pale scar across her lips, and steady hazel eyes. She wears practical chain, a slate cloak, and a horn at her hip, and is rarely seen without a mug of watch-tea.
Personality: stern, methodical, skeptical, and quietly kind. She treats every traveler as a potential threat and every returner as a potential stranger. She has lost too many people to the Woods to take it lightly and hates the forest with a soldier's patience.
Speech: flat, brisk, procedural. "Names. Route. Expected return. And if you come back with one more in your party than you left with, you'll stop right there and wait for the priest."
Role: controls who enters and leaves the Woods and keeps the Registry. She knows every guide in Skyreach, including Stravinsky.
Secret: three months ago a caravan returned with one more traveler than left. The extra was a young girl who knew all the travelers' names. Ilse sent her to the Temple of Helm, and the girl vanished from a locked cell overnight. Ilse has told only Brother Anselm.

93.content:
Wren Ashby (half-elf, 35) runs the Trailhouse and is one of the best rangers in Skyreach. She is lean and wiry, with tanned skin, short brown hair full of pine needles, a crooked nose, and sharp grey-green eyes. She wears worn leather and green wool, a longbow on her back, and bells braided into her hair.
Personality: laconic, practical, dry-humored, and calm. She has guided travelers and hunted in the Woods for fifteen years. She is happiest among trees and least comfortable in crowds. She respects anyone who listens and has no patience for bravado.
Speech: few words, quiet, dry. "The forest isn't evil. It's hungry. Big difference. Mind your feet."
Role: runs the Trailhouse, sells supplies, guides travelers, and keeps the Woods map. She works with Stravinsky but considers him a showman.
Secret: she was raised partly in the Deep Woods by her elven mother, who walked into the forest when Wren was twelve and never came out. Sometimes Wren hears her mother's voice calling from the trees, and she has never answered.

94.content:
Old Moss (firbolg, age unknown) is the druid who tends the Shrine of Silvanus, Rootfather's Stone. He is huge and slow-moving, with blue-grey skin, a broad cow-like nose, drooping ears, and a long beard tangled with moss, twigs, and small sleeping beetles. He wears a cloak of living lichen and carries a staff that has sprouted leaves.
Personality: gentle, slow, patient, and deeply strange. He speaks rarely and in riddles, communes with animals and trees, and regards the city with puzzled tolerance. He is kind to all living things and protective of the Woods.
Speech: slow, deep, cryptic. "The forest... is not angry. It is... listening. You should... listen back."
Role: blesses travelers, reads the mood of the Woods, and sometimes warns of danger. He is the only person who claims to have spoken with the Man of the Trees.
Secret: he knows the Deep Woods is a single vast consciousness, and that the old bargain between Skyreach's founder and the mountain stone is connected to it. The forest has grown restless because the bargain is failing.

95.content:
Magistrate-Envoy Cassius Dravon (human, 45) is Valerius's ambassador to Skyreach, resident at the Valerian Embassy. He is tall and severe, with olive skin, black hair cut short, clean-shaven, and cold dark eyes. He wears structured Valerian blue and grey with a high collar and silver buttons, and the iron badge of the Magistrate Conclave. He never raises his voice and never smiles with his eyes.
Personality: disciplined, intelligent, polite, and controlled. He believes absolutely in Valerian order and regards Skyreach's tolerance of magic, gambling, and "unbound" adventurers as dangerous chaos. Yet he is no cartoon villain: he genuinely wants to prevent another war and is fascinated, despite himself, by Skyreach's freedom.
Speech: formal, measured, clinical. "In Valerius, we do not lock our doors, because there is nothing behind them to fear. Here you lock everything, and still you are afraid. Interesting."
Agenda: renegotiate the Iron Accord, gather intelligence on Skyreach's divination magic and the First Flame, and watch the Pass. He has repeatedly requested access to the Great Library's Restricted Vault.
Secret: Valerius believes the First Flame is a magical binding that could be broken. Cassius has orders to learn how, and he is torn about obeying. He also knows Lord Kaelen Strong's war crime and has discovered Captain Saoirse Deane's privateer past, and he plans to use both.

96.content:
Lady Amarante Solise (human, 32) is a daughter of one of Sunderland's Great Houses and an envoy of the Merchant-Lord Council, staying at the Gilded Gull. She is strikingly beautiful, with honey-gold skin, dark hair coiled with pearls, and warm amber eyes. She wears elegant embroidered wool, a fine cloak, and gemstones she claims are "modest."
Personality: gracious, witty, charming, and politically razor-sharp, a master of Sunderland etiquette and subtle manipulation. She fears social disgrace more than any blade. She enjoys Skyreach's bluntness as a novelty but considers its nobles clumsy players.
Speech: silken, courteous, layered with double meaning. "In Sunderland we have a saying: the lake reflects everything, but shows nothing of its depths. I find Skyreach so refreshingly shallow. I mean that as a compliment, of course."
Agenda: negotiate favorable trade terms and secure Sunderland's interest in the Pass. She is courting both Lord Damon Vantor (a trade alliance) and Lord Chancellor Ashgrove (whose debts her family holds).
Secret: the Deepwake serpent has surfaced in Glassmere Lake, and Sunderland's Great Houses are quietly preparing for disaster. She has been sent to secure Skyreach as a safe haven for Sunderland wealth, and she is under orders to buy the Ashgrove debt so Sunderland effectively owns Skyreach's Mint.

97.content:
Jory "Tide" Malloy (half-elf, 29) is an information broker and trader from Twinharbor who splits his time between the Gilded Gull and the Drowned Lantern. He is lanky and handsome in a rumpled way, with tousled sandy hair, a quick grin, a sunburned nose, and a waterproof Twinharbor greatcoat full of hidden pockets. He wears a sea-glass charm for luck and carries a small slate on which he scribbles constantly.
Personality: fast-talking, charming, opportunistic, and cheerful. He treats information as currency and every conversation as a trade. He is loyal to his guild (the Bridgewardens' Messengers), loves a gamble, and has a soft heart he hides badly.
Speech: rapid, slangy, Twinharbor idioms. "Tide waits for no one, friend. You've got something I want, I've got something you need. Let's not drown in politeness."
Agenda: buy and sell information, arrange cargo, scout opportunities for Twinharbor's guilds, and keep an eye on Vex.
Secret: he is secretly an agent of one of Twinharbor's Underwave Syndicates, sent to broker their alliance with Vex. He has also started to like Skyreach, and Thorfin Brannock's stew, too much.

98.content:
Kaga Breathwalker (goliath, 26) is a young goliath from a clan near Glassmere Falls, newly come to Skyreach as a mercenary. She is seven and a half feet tall, with grey stone-patterned skin, white hair in thick braids, pale blue eyes, and clan markings like rivulets of water. She wears furs and hide armor, carries a greataxe, and wears a vial of mist from Glassmere Falls around her neck.
Personality: earnest, competitive, proud, and curious about city life. She is honest to a fault and baffled by lies, politics, and money. She treats every challenge as a test and every friend as a clan sibling, and she is quick to laugh and quick to anger.
Speech: direct, formal, simple, using goliath idioms. "You are small, but you fight with your whole heart. Good. I will call you friend. Now, what is this 'tax'?"
Agenda: earn glory and coin, prove herself in the Stormfather's Games, and find a warrior named Hrolf, who once fled her clan.
Secret: her clan's elders sent her to warn Skyreach. The Breath of the Mountain has turned cold and bitter, and the mountain spirits are stirring in the frozen canyons. No one in the city has taken her seriously yet.

99.content:
Ithariel (elf, 240, appears about 30) is a scholar and envoy from Silverleaf, studying at the Great Library. He is slender and graceful, with pale silver hair, dark-brown skin, violet eyes, and long-fingered hands stained with ink. He wears flowing green-and-silver robes inappropriate for the cold and is always slightly chilled.
Personality: curious, courteous, absent-minded, and quietly melancholy. He is fascinated by human urgency and finds Skyreach's constant vigilance both admirable and exhausting. He is polite to everyone and condescending without realizing it.
Speech: lyrical, precise, slightly archaic. "Your people build walls against what they fear. Mine, I think, simply waited until it forgot us. I am not certain which is wiser."
Agenda: officially, to research ancient trade with Skyreach. Unofficially, Silverleaf sent him to learn why the Deep Woods, which border elven lands, have grown restless and hostile.
Secret: Silverleaf records describe the original pact between Aethelred and the "stone that remembers." Ithariel has one fragment and is searching for the rest, and he is beginning to suspect that Skyreach's founder broke a promise to the Deep Woods.

100.content:
Sunderland's wealthy, politically shrewd people prize opportunity and use deception for influence. Masters of etiquette, insight, and subtle manipulation, they fear social exile more than legal punishment. Trade is paramount; oaths are sealed at sacred Glassmere Lake.
This refined realm of rolling fields and pale stone is nominally led by the Merchant-Lord Council, but true power resides with the Great Houses. The Court of Etiquette quietly enforces social law, making influence the true currency. Glassmere Lake, a mirrorlike inland sea fed by mountain falls, is a vital trade route, oath-site, and home to the legendary Deepwake lake serpent, whose surfacing portends disaster.
Sunderland's culture blends merchant ambition with mountain caution. Clothing is practical yet elegant (embroidered wool, fine cloaks, gemstones and pearls). Cuisine features grilled lakefish, barley-leek stew, smoked goat, dwarven cheeses, lake ale, and spiced berry wine. Faith honors Waukeen, Gond, and Oghma (The Waters' Promise). Governed by the Merchant-Lord Council and institutions like the Harbor Guilds, they ally with Karak Varn, Twinharbor, and Skyreach, while cautiously engaging Silverleaf and Brightwater.
From Skyreach: Sunderland is Skyreach's closest ally and largest trading partner, reached by mountain roads that open at the Thaw Fair. Sunderland wine, cheese, and fashion are prized by Skyreach nobles, and Sunderland money is quietly buying influence in the city through Lady Amarante Solise and the debts of House Ashgrove.

101.content:
Twinharbor is populated by tough, pragmatic, opportunity-driven people: fast-talking negotiators skilled in persuasion, deception, and streetwise insight. They treat information as currency and risk as routine. Loyalty is to the guild, and their mantra is "The tide waits for no one," shaping a culture of speed and hard bargaining. Alliances are sworn with a Dock Oath in seawater, and true power lies in the hidden triangle of the official Council, the City Watch, and the Underwave Syndicates.
The city is a salt-stained metropolis where the Kallun and Stone Rivers meet the White Sea, built on the convergence of waters, trade routes, and competing ambitions. It is anchored by the Great Bridge of Union, linking the diplomatic North Harbor and the black-market South Harbor, a duality celebrated at the Convergence Festival. Governance is transactional: the Harbormoot sets official policy, but real authority constantly shifts between the Harbor Council, Bridge Wardens, and Underwave Syndicates. "One cup for the law, one cup for the sea" defines its perpetual balancing act.
Twinharbor's culture prizes speed, practicality, and advantage. Bargaining is expected, gossip is fast, and guild identity shapes social life. Worship centers on Gond, Valkur, and Waukeen, with numerous small shrines to luck. Cuisine is diverse and trade-driven (eel pie, chowder, fried shrimp, honey rolls), and clothing favors heavy, waterproof coats. As the indispensable gateway between Sunderland's inland wealth and the ocean's vast opportunities, Twinharbor thrives on motion, negotiation, and the ever-turning tide.
From Skyreach: Twinharbor is reached by ship through the Narrow Pass and around the Broken Shoals (ten to twelve days), or overland through the Deep Woods with a licensed guide (four to five days). Twinharbor traders crowd Breakwater Docks, and its Underwave Syndicates are courting Vex of the Sewer Rats.

102.content:
Valerius is a kingdom built on absolute control, order, and discipline, fiercely hostile to magic and chaos, which they see as the root of all evil. Citizens are raised in state academies to ensure loyalty, emotions are strictly controlled, and magic is heavily regulated and feared by the Arcanum Registry. Rising from black stone ruins, the realm is a fortress of rigid streets, patrolled by the heavily armored Ironwatch Sentinels.
Life is secure and structured; citizens fulfill assigned roles, and public displays are limited to the martial Parade of Steel. Valerians value civic duty and predictability, wearing structured blue, white, and gray, and worship Azuth, Tyr, and Helm. Governed by the Magistrate Conclave, Valerius maintains tense relations with Elderbark and Stonewatch, rivals Skyreach, and stands as a bulwark against chaos through strict law and relentless vigilance.
From Skyreach: Valerius is Skyreach's great rival. The two fought the Pass War (585–587 AF), which ended in the Iron Accord. Valerian ships pass the Narrow Pass daily at fixed tolls, the Valerian Embassy stands in the Noble Quarter, and Envoy Cassius Dravon represents the Magistrate Conclave. Skyreachers and Valerians share the worship of Helm and Tyr but interpret both very differently, and calling someone "Valerian" is an insult in Skyreach.

103.content:
Known as the Crown of Stone, the North Mountains rise in jagged majesty above Skyreach and Sunderland, their peaks and valleys holding wonders and dangers found nowhere else. At Glassmere Falls, glacial melt thunders into Glassmere Lake, filling the air with mist that mountain goliaths call the Breath of the Mountain and regard as sacred. Farther along the range, the Skycliff Aerie cuts across a line of sheer cliffs where giant eagles with wingspans wider than longships make their nests. The bravest climbers leave offerings of meat or fish at the cliff's edge in hopes of seeing one soar. In the northeast, frozen canyons twist into a labyrinth where wind-driven walls of snow shift overnight, opening paths and erasing others without warning. Expeditions vanish into this frosted maze, their campfires swallowed by ice and silence.
From Skyreach: the mountains loom directly above the city and send down the cold wind called the Fang. They supply Skyreach's iron ore, timber, goat, and goliath mercenaries. Two Royal Army patrols have recently vanished near the frozen canyons, and goliath clans report that the Breath of the Mountain has turned cold and bitter.

104.content:
The Deep Woods is an ancient and perilous forest located south of Skyreach, primarily serving as a critical yet highly dangerous trade shortcut to the port city of Twinharbor. It is a primeval entity, a domain older than any recorded kingdom or border, and locals regard it with the profound respect one gives to a destructive force of nature. Economically, Twinharbor profits greatly from the woods, supplying guides, hunting contracts, and salvage from lost caravans, while the powerful city of Skyreach treats the area as a tolerated hazard crucial for commerce but not worth the effort of full conquest.
Entering the Deep Woods is to step into a perpetual twilight, where the dense canopy reduces sunlight to a mere suggestion and the air carries an unusual metallic tang beneath the scent of pine. The atmosphere is deeply unsettling: sound distorts, with strange echoes and footsteps that do not match the walker, fueling the pervasive sense that "The Forest Watches" and that travelers are constantly being measured by an unseen consciousness.
From Skyreach: the Woods begin a bowshot beyond the Southern Gate. Every traveler registers at the Guides' Registry, leaves an offering at Rootfather's Stone, and hires a licensed guide such as Stravinsky. Guides' rules: never leave the path, never answer a voice you cannot see, never sleep without a bell-ward, and never count the travelers aloud. Prince-Consort Tobias vanished here five years ago.

105.content:
Nestled in the southern foothills of the North Mountains, the Stonewood Grove is defined by ancient oaks whose bark has petrified into dense, layered stone that is cool to the touch and harder than steel. The grove is unnaturally still, and its air smells of metallic sap and old moss. Folklore claims that a presence called the Man of the Trees moves within the petrified trunks, drawing lost travelers deeper into the grove until no path leads them home.
From Skyreach: the grove lies where the North Mountains meet the Deep Woods, a place where stone and forest blur together. Scholars in the Great Library's Restricted Vault have linked the Man of the Trees to Skyreach's founding, and Old Moss of the Shrine of Silvanus claims to have spoken with it.

106.content:
The Broken Shoals is a stretch of jagged reefs and half-submerged rocks off the Deep Woods coast, littered with the wrecks of countless ships. At low tide, splintered hulls and leaning masts rise from the surf like skeletal fingers. Lanterns drift through the mist after dark. Some are carried by fishermen who know the channels; others move where no boat should be able to pass.
From Skyreach: ships bound for Twinharbor must sail around the Shoals, and the Iron Accord forbids Skyreach or Valerius from fortifying them. A hidden channel through the reefs is being used by the Sewer Rats and Vantor ships to dodge Pass tolls. Wreck salvage turns up in the Underflow Market, and Windcaller Morwen Salt hears the drowned singing beneath the reefs.
